subject: How to output the geno data after imputation?

messages.author: 963b6d84a823404f
messages.subject: How to output the geno data after imputation?
parts:
I received the email below; I thought I'd start sending such emails and my response to the R/qtl discussion group.

------------

I'm trying to fill the missing genotype data using <- sim.geno at step=1, but after the imputation, how to output the geno data? I tried write.table or print, but both failed.

> print(g)
This is an object of class "cross".
It is too complex to print, so we provide just this summary.

> write.table(g, file="C:/Users/output/f21.csv",sep=",")
Error in as.data.frame.default(x[[i]], optional = TRUE, stringsAsFactors = stringsAsFactors) :
cannot coerce class 'c("f2", "cross")' into a data.frame

Another question is

n.draws=64 is large enough assuming there is no computer burden?

Thanks in advance!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] How to output the geno data after imputation?
parts:
The multiple imputations are not intended to be output to a file, but only used in functions like scanone and effectplot.

The main difficulty in writing them to a file will be that they constitute a 3-dimensional table: individual x position x imputation. They are split apart by chromosome in the cross object; see page 44 in the R/qtl book (http://www.rqtl.org/book).

You can use the function pull.draws to pull them out as a 3-dimensional array, but it's not obvious how to write these to a file.

> data(hyper)
> hyper <- sim.geno(hyper, step=2, n.draws=64)
> dr <- pull.draws(hyper)
> dim(dr)
[1] 250 810 64

Regarding the second question, "is n.draws=64 large enough?" It depends on (a) what you're trying to do and (b) how dense and complete your genotype data are. In general, I'd say, do the imputations again and look at how much the final results change. If they don't change substantially, then you're probably doing sufficient imputations.

karl
